item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 141740
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Wed Oct 14 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located a couple hundred miles south-southeast of the
southern tip of the Baja California peninsula, and on Tropical Storm
Trudy, located several hundred miles south of Acapulco, Mexico.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Public Advisory Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 142045
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Trudy Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 PM CST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
...TRUDY CONTINUES TO STRENGTHEN...
...RESIDENTS OF SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO SHOULD CONTINUE
TO MONITOR THE PROGRESS OF THIS SYSTEM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...11.9N 100.0W
ABOUT 345 MI...555 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 570 MI...915 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...997 MB...29.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in southwestern and west-central Mexico should monitor the 
progress of Trudy. Watches will likely be required tonight or 
Thursday for portions of these areas.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Trudy was
located near latitude 11.9 North, longitude 100.0 West. Trudy is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A turn
toward the northwest is expected tonight, followed by a turn 
toward the north-northwest on Thursday. On the forecast track,
Trudy could approach the coast of southwestern Mexico on Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 65 mph (100 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Steady to rapid strengthening is forecast during 
the next couple of days, and Trudy is forecast to become a major 
hurricane on Friday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 997 mb (29.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.

RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to 
produce 2 to 4 inches with isolated higher totals around 6 inches 
along the southwest Mexican coast between Guerrero and Jalisco. This 
rainfall may result in localized flash flooding, especially in areas 
along steep terrain.

SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico late this week and
continue through the weekend. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 141456
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Trudy Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 AM CST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
Trudy continues to gradually become better organized.  Geostationary
satellite images show a cold central convective area, with the
low-level center likely underneath the western portion of this
convection, although there have only been a couple of microwave
passes over the past 6 to 12 hours, so confidence in the initial
position is still not particularly high.  Trudy also has loosely
connected outer curved convective bands to the northeast and west.
The latest subjective Dvorak estimate from TAFB is 3.5/55 kt, while
objective estimates from UW-CIMSS have been ranging from 36 to 45
kt.  The intensity is increased to 50 kt for this advisory, since
the latest satellite images show continued gradual improvement in
the convective organization.
 
Trudy has been moving toward the west-northwest, or 290/11 kt, to
the south of a mid-level ridge that extends over central Mexico.
However, the ridge is expected to weaken by tomorrow, as Trudy moves
closer to Hurricane Simon.  The two tropical cyclones, which are
currently about 700 n mi apart, are forecast to be within 500 miles
of each other by hour 36, possibly close enough to influence each
other's steering.  By Thursday, increasing mid- to upper-level
troughiness in the west-central Gulf of America and steering from
potential interaction with Simon should cause Trudy to turn
north-northwestward, and possibly northward for a time Thursday
night or Friday.  As Simon finally moves northwest and weakens late
in the forecast period, it should allow the ridge to build back in
and induce Trudy to make a leftward turn back toward the northwest.
There remains significant track spread among the models, but there
has been an overall rightward shift in the model guidance, mainly
during the first 60 to 72 h of the forecast, so the new NHC track
forecast is well to the east of the previous one through 72 h. The
NHC track forecast is slightly to the west of the HCCA and GDMI at
36-72 h.  At day 5, the NHC forecast is slightly south of the
previous one, but well to the north of the latest GDMI, HCCA, and
TVCN, but the forecast that far out is highly uncertain.
 
Environmental conditions continue to look quite favorable along
Trudy's track through the next 60 hours, and the NHC forecast
continues to call for rapid intensification.  By hour 72, there is
increasing confidence that Trudy will reach stronger southwesterly
wind shear, which should induce significant weakening by days 4 and
5, regardless of how much land interaction Trudy incurs.  The NHC
intensity forecast is at the high end of the model guidance
throughout the entire 5-day period, and is similar to the HCCA and
Google DeepMind Ensemble Mean.
 
NHC continues to call for Trudy to get close to the coast of Mexico
as a major hurricane, and given the track uncertainty, residents of
southwestern and west-central Mexico should continue to closely
monitor the progress of Trudy, and be ready to possibly implement
their hurricane plan.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico late this week and
into the weekend. There is an increasing risk of wind, rain, and
storm surge impacts, and watches could be required for a portion of
these areas later today or tonight.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  15/0000Z 12.1N 100.4W   60 KT  70 MPH
 24H  15/1200Z 12.9N 101.2W   75 KT  85 MPH

item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 141447
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 AM MST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
...SIMON WEAKENS WHILE DRIFTING SOUTHWESTWARD...
...INTERESTS IN WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO AND BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR SHOULD
CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.7N 108.1W
ABOUT 165 MI...260 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 250 MI...400 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 230 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...975 MB...28.80 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Government of Mexico has discontinued the Hurricane Watch for
Las Islas Marias.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in west-central Mexico and in Baja California Sur should
continue to monitor Simon. Watches or warnings may be required
for portions of Baja California Sur over the next day or two.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 19.7 North, longitude 108.1 West. Simon is moving
toward the southwest near 2 mph (4 km/h). The hurricane is likely to
move slowly and erratically during the next day or two. A turn 
toward the north or north-northwest is forecast to occur by Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are now near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Some intensity fluctuations are possible through Thursday
night, followed by weakening on Friday and into the weekend.
 
Simon is a very small hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend
outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the center and
tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 975 mb (28.80 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?key_messages.
 
RAINFALL: Through early Saturday, Simon is expected to produce
rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3
inches over portions of the state of Baja California Sur.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast of
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 AM MST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
First-light visible imagery indicates that Simon has continued to
lose organization during the last several hours. The low-level
center is now located near the northern edge of the convective
overcast due to the effects of northerly shear. However, there is
still no microwave imagery of the storm to better diagnose the
internal structure. The satellite intensity estimates have trended
down, and based on this the initial intensity is reduced to a
possibly generous 80 kt.
 
The hurricane continues drifting southwest or 230/2 kt. For the
next day or two, Simon is likely to continue drifting southwestward
in an area of light steering currents, with the center remaining
well offshore. After that time, the track forecast becomes less
confident. While all of the global models agree that a mid- to
upper-level trough should form west of Baja California after 48 h,
there is poor agreement on the track forecasts for Simon during
this time. The GFS and the regional hurricane models forecast that
Simon will continue moving southward or southwestward through 72 h,
followed by a slow movement toward the northwest. The remainder of
the guidance favors a northwestward or north-northwestward turn
between 36-48 h, with that motion continuing through the end of the
forecast period. The new track forecast follows the latter scenario 
in anticipation that the center will try to follow convective bursts 
displaced to the north by southerly shear. The new forecast track is 
again adjusted west of the previous track, but it lies to the east 
of the HCCA corrected consensus and the Google DeepMind ensemble 
mean.
 
Simon's small size makes it susceptible to intensity fluctuations
based on the state of its compact inner core and small changes in
the environmental conditions. The current northerly shear is
forecast to diminish during the next 12-24 h, which may allow some
modest re-intensification. By 36 h, increasing southerly to
southwesterly upper-level flow between the trough to the northwest
and Tropical Storm Trudy to the southeast should cause significant
shear and aid in the entrainment of dry air. This should cause
steady weakening, with Simon expected to weaken to a tropical storm
as it approaches Baja California Sur. The system is likely to decay
to a remnant low by 120 h as the shear and dry air cause the
convection to dissipate.
 
Simon continues to be a challenging storm to forecast, and
confidence remains lower than normal given the weak steering,
proximity to land, very small size, and significant model spread.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. While Simon is no longer expected to bring hurricane conditions
to Las Islas Marias, interests in west-central Mexico and Baja
California Sur should continue to closely monitor the latest
updates. Watches or warnings could be required for portions of Baja
California Sur over the next day or two.
 
2. Large swells will likely affect portions of the coast of
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur over the next several
days. These swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.
